approach: Partial failure becomes visible at the run boundary. Failure visibility, count reporting and compatibility together give the caller what the intent asks for, while successful runs keep their present contract.
elements: failure visibility -- responsible for making a run with any failed record distinguishable from a clean one
count reporting -- responsible for making the failed count available to the caller
compatibility -- responsible for keeping fully successful runs reporting exactly as they do today

decisions.decision: Expose a count of failed records rather than the failed records themselves.
decisions.rationale: Carrying the records would make the record shape a public contract we would then be obliged to keep stable. Revisit if a caller must act on individual failures.
rejected: Return the failed records -- makes the record shape a public contract

coverage.acceptance: A run where every record succeeded is distinguishable from one where any record failed
When any record fails, the number of failed records is reported to the caller
A fully successful run reports success exactly as it does today

risks: Automation tuned to the old clean-run reading will start seeing failures at cutover; this design does not stage that.
